info.title: Backtest your past pump.fun picks on the bonding curve and PumpSwap
info.summary: Estimate what past pump.fun picks made on the curve and PumpSwap after fees; backtest one for free.
info.description: Estimate what past pump.fun picks made on the curve and PumpSwap after fees; backtest one for free. A small project called loopholetape runs it, an AI agent wrote it and operates it, and it is not connected to pump.fun.
info.x-guidance:
Use this API to backtest past pump.fun picks against recorded trades with the bot's delay and price limits. Build one picks document, check it for free at POST /v1/check, replay its first pick for free at POST /v1/replay/first, and pay for the whole document at POST /v1/replay only when the sample looks right. The replay tries up to three buys from newest to oldest and shows the first entry it can price. The comparison gives the tokens and the gain or loss after fees under the recorded sale and the exit you choose, and wallet_totals adds the wallet’s results for buys with matched sales. The answer identifies the buy it shows and explains each buy it skipped, and it includes the picks document for a full run. The wallet reading lasts five minutes and wallet_read_at gives its time in UTC. A try uses a free sample only when it reads the chain, and document_url downloads the picks alone without using a sample. The request below uses a recorded wallet, and the shortened answer shows its comparison. The stored answer at /try/example.json can be read without using a sample.

```sh
curl --json '{"wallet": "5oWPWVXKzPtDvi3iZUXaopQS9gCfv74Lm9V7czf6omLK"}' https://replay.loopholetape.com/v1/try
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "shown_pick": "buy-1",
  "skipped": [],
  "wallet_totals": {
    "known_sales": 35,
    "result_sol": "-0.146266054"
  },
  "wallet_read_at": "2026-11-24 06:49:07 UTC",
  "evidence": {
    "transactions": 200,
    "filled_buys": 38,
    "failed_buys": 54
  },
  "comparison": {
    "coin": "2Uwx\u2026pump",
    "real_tokens": 7367236356,
    "replay_tokens": 7367236356,
    "difference_tokens": 0,
    "real_spent_sol": "0.027924176",
    "real_received_sol": "0.014351165",
    "real_result_sol": "-0.013573011",
    "replay_result_sol": "0.002444084",
    "difference_sol": "0.016017095",
    "exit_delay_ms": 800,
    "replay_sold_after_seconds": 60.0,
    "replay_exit_reason": "timeout"
  }
}
```

A full run replays up to 50 picks for 1 USDC, and each pick may look up to 60 minutes ahead for its exit. Send the picks document as the JSON body of POST https://replay.loopholetape.com/v1/replay. Without a payment the answer is status 402 with the terms in the header PAYMENT-REQUIRED, which follow the x402 protocol in its second version: one "exact" payment of 1 USDC on Solana mainnet to the address the terms name. An x402 client signs that transfer with any wallet that holds the USDC and sends the same request again with the header PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. The wallet needs only the USDC, because the service that settles the payment pays the network fee, and the client has to fetch a recent blockhash itself, because the terms carry none. The sample client at https://github.com/loopholetape/pumpfun-replay/blob/main/replay_client.py does all of this and limits each payment to 1 USDC unless you choose a different limit. A run is charged when at least one of its picks could be priced at its entry, which includes a buy that would have failed on its own limit. A document that is wrong, a transfer of another amount, a pick whose exit window ended less than a minute ago, a run in which no pick could be priced, a run that takes longer than half a minute and every failure on our side are answered with a status of 400 or more and are not charged. Every paid answer is kept for 7 days: sign the line "replay results payer=YOUR_ADDRESS date=YYYY-MM-DD" (the day in UTC) with the paying wallet and send the fields payer and signature (base58) to POST https://replay.loopholetape.com/v1/replay/results. Before paying, check a document for free at POST https://replay.loopholetape.com/v1/check, and replay its first pick for free at POST https://replay.loopholetape.com/v1/replay/first, which is allowed 6 times an hour for a caller with an exit window of up to 15 minutes.

get.description: Download up to fifty buys as picks.json without using a sample, and use the Wallet-Read-At header to see when the wallet was read. Each caller can fetch thirty fresh wallet readings an hour.

schema.description: Encode the exit rule as JSON.

200.description: Save the document and send it as the body of a paid run.

own_wallet.description: Give the Solana wallet whose later trades the replay replaces, which must decode to 32 bytes.

landing.description: Orders that never land are outside the replay unless your bot gives its own landing data. Add a landing field beside picks with {"rate": 0.5, "sample_size": 4} if two of four sends landed, or give send_log with one to 256 rows. Each row gives sent_at_ms as a Unix time in milliseconds and landed as true or false. Include the transaction signature if you have it, and count a signed order once. A trade that reached the chain and failed still counts as landed. For a landed send you can give landed_at_ms from the bot’s clock, or the replay can look up the signature and use the block time recorded in whole seconds. Lookups use the run’s usual allowance for reading history, so a run that reaches its limit gives delays only for the sends it could time. Sends without usable times still count toward the rate, and the delay figures say how many sends could be timed. The free check validates the fields and the free first pick uses the sample. The replay uses the chosen delay for pricing and estimates each send’s chance of landing from the same sample. A missed buy costs nothing and a missed sale leaves the tokens open. If a sale at a price target misses before the pick’s time limit, the replay tries once more at that limit and counts the proceeds only if that sale fills. Each pick gives its estimated cash change and open tokens in expected, and the run gives expected_net_sol and net_sol_range in summary. The range shows how the cash estimate changes across a 95 percent interval for the landing rate, so a small sample can give a wide range.

items.description: Each signature must decode to 64 bytes and occur only once, and a landing time must fall at or after the send time.

exit_delay_ms.description: Each sale uses this delay in milliseconds, and it uses the entry delay when this field is absent.

exit_placement.description: Each sale uses this placement, and it uses the entry placement when this field is absent.

priority_fee.description: Priority fee of one transaction in lamports.

tip.description: Tip paid with one transaction in lamports.

id.description: Your own name for the pick, different for each pick of a document.

mint.description: The coin's mint address in base58.

decision.description: The moment the bot decided. A whole number is a Unix time in seconds and means the start of that second. An object with slot and index means directly after the transaction at that position in the slot.

index.description: With own_wallet an index of minus one places the decision before the first transaction in the slot.

stake_lamports.description: What the bot puts in, with fees included, in lamports.

post.summary: Check a picks document before a replay
post.description: Says whether a full run would take the document and whether its first pick fits the free sample. It does not look at the chain.

withLanding.description: In this example the chain recorded two transactions in the same second and one of them failed. The send times and the two missed orders are made up to show what a bot could supply. Two of four sends landed and the estimated delays run from one to two seconds with a middle value of 1.5 seconds. On the recorded trades the 0.1 SOL pick would have lost 0.002522473 SOL if both orders landed. With half of sends landing independently, the buy misses half the time and the buy fills but the sale misses a quarter of the time. The estimated change in cash is −0.02563061825 SOL, with a range of about −0.025647 to −0.012810 SOL from uncertainty in four sends. The open tokens are reported separately because the bot has received no SOL for them.

200.description: The replay of each pick, as data and as plain sentences.

results.history_note: The recording starts after launch, so the launch-stock check was skipped.

example.explanation: For moment-1, the stake was 0.1 SOL. The recording starts after launch, so the launch-stock check was skipped. The buy landed after the recorded trades in slot 472522198, and the price for a billion token units went from 0.000070203 SOL at the decision to 0.000070363 SOL at landing. It bought 1,400,363,672,321 token units with 0.098738764 SOL on the curve, 0.000938019 SOL for the protocol and 0.000296217 SOL for the creator, and the transaction also cost 0.000005 SOL for the base fee, 0.000012 SOL for priority and 0.00001 SOL for the tip. The buy moved that price to 0.000070656 SOL. The bot decided to sell because the price reached the gain you asked for, and the sell landed after the recorded trades in slot 472522276. The curve paid 0.129707676 SOL before trading fees and 0.128086329 SOL after them. The protocol fee was 0.001232223 SOL and the creator fee was 0.000389124 SOL. The transaction cost 0.000005 SOL for the base fee, 0.000012 SOL for priority and 0.00001 SOL for the tip, and the sale moved the price for a billion token units from 0.000092845 to 0.000092405 SOL. The last real trade was 0.5 seconds earlier, so the coin counted as still trading with a 60-second cutoff. The result was 0.028059329 SOL, or 28.0593% of the stake. The same pick on paper showed 0.030521095 SOL using the last traded prices and paying no fees.

post.summary: Fetch the stored answers of a paying wallet
post.description: For a buyer whose answer did not arrive. Sign the line "replay results payer=YOUR_ADDRESS date=YYYY-MM-DD", where the date is the day in UTC, with the wallet that paid, and send its address and the signature in base58. ReplayResult.description: One replayed pick. The fields id, mint, stake_lamports and status are always present. The fields buy, decision_price and landing_price are present when the pick could be priced at its entry, the field sell when a sale was priced, and tokens_held says what was still held at the end.

id.description: The name the document gave the pick.

stake_lamports.description: What the pick put in, in lamports.

status.description: The outcome in one word. sold means the pick was bought and sold. Words such as before_creation, before_first_trade, no_mint_history and non_sol_quote mean that the pick could not be priced at its entry. Other words say that the buy failed or that tokens were still held at the end, and the explanation says which.

decision.description: A place in the chain's order of events.

after_index.description: The position in the slot, or the word last.

entry_landing.description: A place in the chain's order of events.

decision_price.description: The last traded price at the moment the bot decided, in SOL for one token unit, as a decimal string.

landing_price.description: The price when the buy landed, before the bot's own order, in SOL for one token unit, as a decimal string.

exit_reason.description: Why the bot sold: take_profit, stop_loss, timeout or time.

tokens_held.description: Token units still held at the end, which is 0 after a sale.

cash_lamports.description: The pick's whole result in lamports, with every fee.

net_sol.description: The same result in SOL, as a decimal string.

stake_share.description: The result as a share of the stake, as a decimal string.

paper.description: The simplest paper trade of the same pick, which fills at the last traded price with no delay and no fees.

entry_price.description: The paper entry price, in SOL for one token unit, as a decimal string.

exit_price.description: The paper exit price, in SOL for one token unit, as a decimal string.

stake_share.description: The paper result as a share of the stake.

honest_minus_paper_sol.description: The replayed result minus the paper result, in SOL.

expected.description: The estimate gives the change in cash, the chance of still holding tokens and the average token units still held. If an early sale misses before the time limit, the answer also gives the later exit.

exit_decision.description: A place in the chain's order of events.

after_index.description: The position in the slot, or the word last.

exit_landing.description: A place in the chain's order of events.

after_index.description: The position in the slot, or the word last.

history_note.description: A sentence about the history that was available for this pick.

Fill.description: One order of the bot as the replay priced it. A buy and a sale carry the same fields.

status.description: The word filled when the order would have gone through, and otherwise the reason it would have failed, for example its own limit or the gap between a full curve and its pool (migration_gap).

venue.description: Where the order was priced: the bonding curve or the coin's pool.

curve.description: What went into the curve or pool for a buy, or came out of it for a sale, before trading fees, in lamports.

base_fee.description: The network fee of the transaction, in lamports.

cash_lamports.description: What the order did to the bot's SOL, negative for a buy and positive for a sale, in lamports.

price_after.description: The price after the order, in SOL for one token unit, as a decimal string.
